games.title: King's Field
games.note: A first-person dungeon crawler released as a launch title for the PlayStation in Japan.

games.title: Bloodborne
games.note: Co-produced with Sony's Japan Studio; its Victorian city of Yharnam draws on Lovecraft and Dracula.

games.title: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
games.note: Won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2019.

games.title: Tenchu: Stealth Assassins
games.note: Released in Japan months before Metal Gear Solid, making it one of the first 3D stealth games.

games.title: Salt and Sanctuary
games.note: Made by Ska Studios, the husband-and-wife team of James and Michelle Silva.

games.title: Nioh
games.note: Began as Oni, an unfinished Akira Kurosawa script; it was first announced in 2004.

games.title: Nioh 3
games.note: Less linear than earlier Nioh games, with larger fields and a switchable samurai or ninja style.

games.title: Code Vein
games.note: Staff from Bandai Namco's God Eater games worked on it.

games.title: The Surge
games.note: You cut specific armor pieces off enemies to craft that gear yourself.

games.title: Lords of the Fallen (2023)
games.note: Players carry a lantern that lets them cross into Umbral, a parallel realm of the dead.

games.title: Remnant: From the Ashes
games.note: Gunfire Games was founded in Austin by David Adams, who had earlier founded Darksiders studio Vigil Games.

games.title: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
games.note: Directed by Stig Asmussen, who had directed God of War III.

games.title: Lies of P
games.note: Retells Collodi's Pinocchio in a Belle Époque city overrun by puppets.

games.title: Black Myth: Wukong
games.note: Based on Journey to the West; it drew over two million players at once on Steam at launch.

games.title: Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty
games.note: Set during the fall of the Han dynasty, drawing on Romance of the Three Kingdoms.

games.title: The First Berserker: Khazan
games.note: Its art style grew out of a cancelled Dungeon Fighter Online prototype called Project BBQ.

games.title: Dungeon Fighter Online
games.note: Hugely popular in China, where it became one of the highest-grossing PC games.

games.title: Blasphemous
games.note: Its Seville studio drew on Spanish Catholic imagery and Andalusian art.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden
games.note: Told its story through cinematic cutscenes between stages, rare in 1988.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden (2004)
games.note: Tomonobu Itagaki's reboot, known for its difficulty; it shares a world with Dead or Alive.

games.title: Onimusha: Warlords
games.note: Actor Takeshi Kaneshiro modeled and voiced the samurai hero Samanosuke.

games.title: Devil May Cry 3: Dante's Awakening
games.note: A prequel that added switchable fighting styles such as Trickster and Swordmaster.

games.title: Bayonetta
games.note: Dodging at the last moment triggers Witch Time, which slows enemies down.

games.title: Bayonetta 2
games.note: Nintendo funded it after the sequel struggled to find a publisher.

games.title: Viewtiful Joe
games.note: Directed by Hideki Kamiya; its team became Capcom's Clover Studio.

games.title: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance
games.note: Kojima Productions' version was cancelled in 2010 before PlatinumGames rebuilt it.

games.title: Hi-Fi Rush
games.note: Revealed and released on the same day by a studio known for horror games.

games.title: Strider
games.note: Its acrobatic hero Hiryu climbs walls and clings to ceilings while slashing with a plasma sword.

games.title: RuneQuest
games.note: A tabletop RPG set in the mythic world of Glorantha, known for skill-based rather than class-based characters.

updates.value: Began as Hideki Kamiya's first take on Resident Evil 4 before becoming a new series.
Players leave messages and bloodstains that appear in strangers' worlds, to warn them or trick them.
George R. R. Martin wrote the backstory that Hidetaka Miyazaki's team built the world on.
